questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A highly rated university, with an international enviroment. Also I thought Edinburgh was very beautiful, and close to the nature in the highlands.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: pretty Easy - lots of e-mails which could be confusing, but there was an orientation week in the beginning of the semester where u could also get information in person and seek out relevant sources.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: e-mails, lots of emails and a guidance counselor specifically for exchange-students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: the orientation overall was very nice, but I would have liked some orientation more specifically targeted exchange students - also a way to get to know the other exchange-students at campus.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: it was hard because there is a general lack of housing in the city because of how many students that are enrolled at the universities. But I was glad I lived off-campus, since you otherwise live with very young people at the dorms given to you by the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was super expensive (both off-campus and on-campus), but in my friendgroup u would be lucky just to get a place to stay there was'nt an even more expensive airBnB - start early!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again very easy - I got all the classes I wanted and had signed up for back home online.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had a online startup meeting with the guidance counselor and then registered at the university with our passport etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The guidance counselor and the many e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: super succesful - I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: read the e-mails, even though there are a lot and reach out if you need help and if you dont understand something - everyone are very friendly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A very nice academic enviroment, I loved all my professors

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two first year courses and one third year which I felt was the perfect combination for an exchange-student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of lectures with a few hundred people and then some exercise-classes with only 8-10 people where you had to show up.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Scottish legal System
International Law
Criminology of Atrocity crimes

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Scottish legal system, very nice for exchange students to do a course on the Scottish law 
Criminology of Atrocity crimes, my favorite course ever, because you were in charge of your own little research project.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food is less expensive, but housing is very expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are really clubs and societies for everything, but it is hard for an exchange student to be a real part of it, because we are only there for one semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: everything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The whiskey society, scandinavian society and the erasmus society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just go to the the highlands as much as possible

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: to be honest it is just easier to talk to international and exchange students because as they are not here for very long either, they have the same mindset as you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, maybe all the beer.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: everyone is very friendly from the staff at the university, to the barmen at the pubs and the busdriver.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
remember to save some money up before you go
be outgoing 
dont expect every day to be amazing - you can also have lonely/boring days on exchange and that is okay

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: during orientation there are a lot of activities you can do, but you have to plan them yourself and there is nothing u "have to do", like in the introweek af CPH where u get put on a team and are forced to do everything with them in the first week. Therefore it maybe takes a while to find the people you connect with, which can be stressful when you are only there for a few months. But remember to be patient and outgoing and just say yes to the things people invite you to.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: independence and english skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: homesickness

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Edinburgh and Scotland are my new favorite places.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
